decision: Reject per-row Python-thread validation for this workload. Restore the full-input-proven production files byte-for-byte; no thread setting or slower path remains in the current production tree.
scope: One complete official Overture source, not complete 32-source throughput or a C++ comparison

experiment.backend: Proper GDAL/OGR Python bindings, independent geometry objects, persistent Python thread pool, source-slot status reassembly
experiment.timing_protocol: Separate exclusive internal window, serial first then threaded, in-process source hashing and pool startup/join included. No source acquisition; pixel comparison excluded.
experiment.repeats: One complete go/no-go pair. The roughly fourfold regression was not repeated or promoted. Cache/outside-host effects remain uncontrolled.

correctness_tests: 130 focused checks passed before the trial, including out-of-order first failures, malformed input, holes, dimensions, pool reuse, failure shutdown, source provenance and no subprocess/ctypes execution.
code_disposition: The rejected prototype and benchmark are not included in the production tree or published as a runtime option. Only the result documents are retained; measured source hashes remain in the receipt to scope this historical observation.
next_direction: Investigate whole-batch geometry metadata/validity through supported GDAL APIs to reduce per-row language-boundary work. The measured regression localizes to parsing/validation/indexing; its exact GIL, allocation or library-lock causes were not isolated. No batch-API gain is claimed yet.
